small_guidance:
- The current kernel recomputes the conv for each of the POOL_K*POOL_K positions independently — this doubles the FLOPs vs. doing conv once then pooling. Restructure so each program tile computes the full conv output for a 2*BLOCK_SP region (the pre-pool tile) once, then reduces with max across pool windows in registers before the mish epilogue.
- BLOCK_K=128 (full IC) forces a single big GEMM-K; try splitting K with BLOCK_K=32 or 64 so the inner `tl.dot` operates on smaller matrices that fit registers better, and tune `(BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP) ∈ {(64,64),(128,64),(64,128)}` with num_warps=8.
- Switch input layout to channels_last (NHWC) so the IC axis is contiguous and loads coalesce across the GEMM-K dimension; this is the canonical conv-as-GEMM layout and will significantly improve memory throughput vs. the current NCHW gather.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per `(N, OC tile, pre-pool output-spatial tile)` computing the full conv output once with `tl.dot` over a `K = IC*KH*KW` reduction. Then fuse hardswish + 2x2 maxpool + mish in the epilogue by having each program output a BLOCK_SP/4 tile of post-pool elements (load 2x2 conv outputs from registers, reduce max, apply mish). This avoids the current 4x redundant conv work.
- Use NHWC layout for the input and OC-outermost weight layout so the K-loop reads contiguous IC chunks; the inner `tl.dot` becomes a clean `(BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K) x (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SP)` GEMM with BLOCK_K=32 unrolled across `(kh, kw, ic_chunk)`.
- Pre-pad the input by 0 on the boundary (or compute valid masks once outside the K-loop) so the inner GEMM has no per-(kh,kw) masking branches; hoist all index math for the pre-pool tile out of the K loop. Wrap in `triton.autotune` keyed on `(OC, OH*OW, IC*KH*KW)` with safe starting tiles `(BM,BN,BK) ∈ {(64,64,32),(128,32,32),(64,128,32)}` at num_warps=4/8, num_stages=2.
